meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'more; still; yet', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for; behind', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Common masculine noun meaning 'nonsense, rubbish (colloq.)' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: What the hell is going on here?
It is not lucky at all!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'such, like this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'between, among', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You two sort it out between yourselves here.
There are no secrets between us.

examples.text: Ну ладно, вы тут между собой договоритесь.
examples.trans: All right, you two sort it out between yourselves here.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('other').

examples.trans: For your information, I am the chairman of the court.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, здесь же ребёнок, мы завтракаем. А телевизор, между прочим, наш!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, there's a child here, we're having breakfast. And the television, by the way, is ours!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

пройти.gloss: to go through, to pass; to come along

meanings.en: to go through, to pass; to come along
meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go through, to pass; to come along', paired with 'проходить'.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to take', paired with 'брать'.

examples.text: Вот и возьмите на работу Галилея.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'обеседование'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'interview' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Завтра у меня важное собеседование на работу.
examples.trans: Tomorrow I have an important job interview.

examples.text: В каком ресторане у тебя собеседование?
examples.trans: At which restaurant is your interview?

проходить.gloss: to go through; to come in

meanings.en: to go through; to come in
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go through; to come in', paired with 'пройти'.

examples.text: Вика, Паша! Как я рад. Проходите, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Vika, Pasha! I'm so glad. Come in, please.

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to excuse; (imperative) sorry, excuse me', paired with 'извинять'.

examples.trans: Thank you, Marina. Sorry, I'm in a hurry.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').
Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common feminine noun meaning 'little mistake' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Шеф, извините меня, пожалуйста, ошибочка вышла.
examples.trans: Chef, please forgive me, there was a little mistake.

выйти.gloss: to go out, to get out

meanings.en: to go out, to get out
meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go out, to get out', paired with 'выходить'.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

принять.gloss: to receive, to see (a visitor); to accept

meanings.en: to receive, to see (a visitor); to accept
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to receive, to see (a visitor); to accept', paired with 'принимать'.

examples.trans: You recognised me. Thanks for seeing me.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to work', paired with 'поработать'.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'two', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in (time); through', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нормально? Она через неделю снова потечёт!
examples.trans: Fine? It'll be leaking again in a week!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'cook, chef' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto; for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.trans: And the kitchen is over there.
We are sitting in the kitchen.

examples.text: Проходите, пожалуйста! Как видите, большой коридор, а там кухня.
examples.trans: Come on in, please! As you can see, a big hall, and the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'beard' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Тогда, наверное, он выпал из бороды.
examples.trans: Then probably it fell out of a beard.

examples.text: У меня нет бороды, позовите шефа!
examples.trans: I do not have a beard, call the chef!

нельзя.gloss: it is not allowed; one can't

meanings.en: it is not allowed; one can't
meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'льзя').

examples.trans: Not allowed? All right, I'll go and do my homework.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem '-первых').

examples.trans: First of all, there hasn't been a trial yet.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem '-вторых').

examples.text: А во-вторых, у меня нет денег.
examples.trans: And secondly, I have no money.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нимать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to understand', paired with 'понять'.

examples.trans: I want to go to the sea, you know?

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'she; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'дача'). Common feminine noun meaning 'luck' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: That's a real stroke of luck.

examples.text: Нет, не получается у меня это забыть. Удачи тебе на новом месте работы.
examples.trans: No, I just can't forget it. Good luck to you in your new job.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'носить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to bring', paired with 'принести'.

examples.text: Я приношу бутылку шампанского и свечи.
examples.trans: I'll bring a bottle of champagne and candles.

examples.text: И не надо больше никаких документов сюда приносить!
examples.trans: And don't bring any more documents in here!
